name: Franco-Nevada
thesis: Franco-Nevada is the purest royalty/streaming compounder in precious metals: it owns price exposure without owning mines, so it bears no operating cost, capex, or labor inflation while collecting top-line revenue off ~430 assets. The model converts a gold bull market almost directly into free cash flow — FY2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 90.9% and OCF was $1,493.7M (+80% YoY) on $1,822.8M revenue, and Q1 2026 already printed $650.7M revenue (+77%), $458.3M adjusted net income (70.4% margin), and a 91.0% EBITDA margin. The company is debt-free with $670.9M cash and ~$3.1B available capital, funding ~$1.8B of 2025 deals (Cote 7.5% GMR for $1,050M; Sibanye Western Limb stream $500M) plus 2026 additions (Gatos-area royalty $225M+, Casa Berardi $100M). The core bet: gold near ~$4,300/oz (off the Jan-2026 ~$5,590 peak; JPMorgan/BofA see ~$6,000 by year-end) keeps flowing through a fixed-cost structure, while 19 straight dividend hikes (now $0.44/qtr) and inflation-protected royalties compound book value. What the market under-models is Cobre Panama optionality — FNV's 2026 guidance of 510k-570k GEOs assumes ZERO restart, yet Panama has suspended arbitration and President Mulino is reopening restart talks; that asset was a >$300M/yr revenue contributor, pure upside not in numbers. What's PRICED IN: at a premium ~1.8x NAV, a high-30s forward P/E and ~0.7% yield, FNV already capitalizes high gold prices and a benign deal environment; the margin of safety is thin if gold mean-reverts toward the $3,000s, and the stock could de-rate even with strong fundamentals. The asymmetry favors patience: this is a great business whose price already embeds peak-commodity FCF plus a Panama win.
key_driver: The realized gold price — with near-zero operating leverage, FNV's free cash flow tracks the gold price almost one-for-one, so the thesis lives or dies on gold holding its $4,000+ regime (Cobre Panama restart is the embedded free call option).

tier_1_kpis.name: Revenue
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Two consecutive quarters of YoY revenue decline outside a falling-gold tape (signals stream/royalty portfolio attrition, not just commodity beta)

tier_1_kpis.name: GEOs sold (gold-equivalent ounces)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: FY GEOs falling below the 510,000 low end of 2026 guidance, signaling portfolio depletion outpacing new deals

tier_1_kpis.name: Adjusted net income margin
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Adjusted margin compressing below ~60% absent a deliberate diversified-deal mix shift (would imply cost/structure creep alien to the royalty model)

tier_1_kpis.name: Operating cash flow
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: TTM OCF declining YoY while gold prices are flat-to-up (decoupling of cash conversion from the model)

tier_1_kpis.name: Net cash / available capital
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Taking on net debt to fund a single deal, or available capital falling below ~$1b without a transformational acquisition to show for it

tier_1_kpis.name: Deal pace (capital deployed on new royalties/streams)
tier_1_kpis.current: ~$1.8b deployed in 2025 (Cote $1,050m GMR; Sibanye Western Limb $500m); 2026 adds Gatos-area royalty ~$225m+ and Casa Berardi $100m stream
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: A full year with <$300m deployed and no pipeline disclosed (reinvestment engine stalling, the long-term growth lever)

tier_2_kpis.current: ~$4,300/oz June 2026 (peaked ~$5,590 on Jan 28, 2026); JPMorgan/BofA target ~$6,000 by year-end 2026

tier_2_kpis.name: Geographic concentration
tier_2_kpis.current: ~84-87% of revenue from the Americas (~41% South America)

tier_2_kpis.current: 510,000-570,000 total GEOs; 360,000-400,000 gold oz; ~90% precious metals — assumes NO Cobre Panama restart

tier_3_kpis.name: Forward P/CF and P/NAV multiple vs. WPM and RGLD

nuance.bear_case: Franco-Nevada at a premium ~1.8x NAV (BMO, Jan 2026) versus miners at 0.7-0.9x, a trailing P/E in the 50s (forward ~34), ~28x sales, and a token ~0.7% yield is priced for a permanent gold supercycle. Q1 2026's 'record' 77% revenue jump and gross-margin/GEO leap from $2,559 to $4,534 were almost entirely price, not volume: gold hit an all-time ~$5,590 (Jan 29, 2026) and has already mean-reverted ~20-25% toward ~$4,100 by late June. Current FCF is cyclically inflated. Concentration is real: Cobre Panama was ~17% of 2022 revenue ($223M), has been shut since late-2023 (a >US$1B impairment), carries zero in 2026 guidance, and a full restart hinges on October-2026 arbitration plus a Panamanian government demanding resource ownership. Meanwhile ~US$1.8B was deployed over two years into a crowded three-firm oligopoly where rising depletion costs signal pricier, lower-return deals. A premium multiple resting on a peaked commodity and a frozen flagship asset is fragile.
nuance.adversarial_take: Bulls are capitalizing trough-of-supply, peak-of-price economics as if they were the through-cycle norm — paying a premium NAV and a high-50s trailing P/E for cash flows that just doubled on a gold spike that has already partially unwound. The mistake is treating Cobre Panama as a free option (zero in guidance, so 'all upside') while ignoring that the same asset already cost a US$1B impairment and is hostage to an arbitration and a government that wants the resource. You are underwriting record gold, a Panama restart, AND accretive redeployment of US$1.8B+ simultaneously. The right posture is Watch, not Buy: the business is genuinely high-quality (no debt, ~90% margins, diversified), but quality at the wrong price is a bad trade. Want it at a normalized-gold P/NAV closer to peers, after the multiple compresses toward 1.3-1.5x NAV on normalized FCF.
nuance.stress_test: Assume gold mean-reverts from ~$4,100 to ~$3,000 (a further ~25%, still historically elevated). Royalty revenue is near-pure margin, so a ~25% price drop flows almost one-for-one to revenue and FCF — the Q1 2026 ~$650M run-rate compresses materially. Layer in Cobre Panama's arbitration slipping past 2026 (full restart pushed to 2028+, keeping ~10-15% of normalized GEOs offline) and one operator (e.g. Candelaria or Antapaccay) trimming output. The market then re-rates a now-shrinking earnings stream off a premium P/E and ~1.8x NAV toward ~1.3x — a double hit of lower numerator and lower multiple, compounding to a 40-50% drawdown from the early-2026 peak.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Gold breaks below ~$3,000/oz and holds, collapsing the price-driven margin/GEO that drove Q1 2026 (from $2,559 to $4,534).
October-2026 Cobre Panama arbitration fails or stalls, with Panama insisting on state resource ownership and no full-restart timeline emerging.
A new acquisition is publicly criticized as dilutive/low-IRR, confirming reinvestment-return compression as rising depletion costs ($77.9M) already hint.
P/NAV multiple compresses toward peers/miners (1.3-1.5x), erasing the structural premium even if gold is flat.
A major operator (Candelaria, Antapaccay, Antamina) announces a production cut, mine-life downgrade, or labor/jurisdiction disruption.
Sell-side fair-value estimates are cut and the 'Buy' consensus flips to Hold as gold normalizes.
Resource nationalism or new royalty/windfall taxes in a key Latin American jurisdiction (~84% of revenue is Americas, ~41% South America) impair stream economics.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — operating loss.
GAAP net income negative for 2 consecutive quarters — bottom-line loss.

business_model_rules.narrative: A royalty/streaming model has no mining opex or capex, so operating margin should sit comfortably above 60% (FNV runs ~70-83%). Two straight quarters below 55% would mean either cost structure is creeping in (alien to the model) or impairments/write-downs are recurring — both undercut the core 'price exposure without operating cost' thesis.

FNV's near-pure-margin royalty economics deliver net margins of ~60-72%. Two consecutive quarters of GAAP net margin below 50% — absent a one-off impairment — would signal the cash-conversion advantage that justifies the premium multiple is eroding (cost creep, sustained write-downs, or stream economics deteriorating).

Given a fixed, growing royalty portfolio and inflation-protected streams, revenue should grow through cycles unless gold collapses or assets deplete. Two consecutive quarters of revenue falling more than 15% YoY would indicate genuine portfolio attrition or a severe commodity-regime change that breaks the compounding story. (NB: FCF-margin and capex/revenue break rules are deliberately omitted — FNV's reported capex line captures lumpy stream/royalty ACQUISITIONS, not sustaining capex, so those ratios swing wildly and would false-breach for a royalty model.)
